# ATT&CK Priority Gap Analysis

<!-- Generated by scripts/build_priority_gaps.py from the ATT&CK v19.2 data and edge tables. Do not edit by hand: edit the script or the data and re-run it. -->

> A data-driven prioritization of MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise techniques (v19.2), combining how often adversaries use a technique (tracked threat-group count) with how thinly the control framework covers it (NIST 800-53 R5 control depth). The result surfaces the techniques that are both widely used and under-covered: the behaviors most worth detection and mitigation investment.

| | |
|---|---|
| Read this when | deciding which ATT&CK techniques to invest detection or mitigation effort in next, justifying control gaps against NIST 800-53 coverage, building a threat-informed roadmap from real adversary usage |
| Start at | [Top 75 priority techniques](#top-75-priority-techniques), [Coverage by tactic](#coverage-by-tactic), [How to use this](#how-to-use-this) |
| Pairs with | [ATTACK_MATRIX_ANALYSIS_REFERENCE.md](/ATTACK_MATRIX_ANALYSIS_REFERENCE.md), [detections/TECHNIQUE_DETECTION_LIBRARY.md](/detections/TECHNIQUE_DETECTION_LIBRARY.md) |

Priority score = `group_count × (1 + 1 / (nist_control_count + 1))`, the same inverse-coverage weighting as the [Risk lens](/ATTACK_MATRIX_ANALYSIS_REFERENCE.md#lens-family-5-breach-patterns-amp-composite-risk). Machine-readable: [`scores/attack_priority_gaps.json`](https://github.com/TeamStarWolf/TeamStarWolf/blob/main/scores/attack_priority_gaps.json).

Generated by `scripts/build_priority_gaps.py` from these inputs (sha256, first 12 hex digits); `--check` exits non-zero when this page or its layers are stale:

- [`data/attack/technique_profiles.jsonl`](https://github.com/TeamStarWolf/TeamStarWolf/blob/main/data/attack/technique_profiles.jsonl) `56c1302b4620`
- [`data/attack/superseded_by.jsonl`](https://github.com/TeamStarWolf/TeamStarWolf/blob/main/data/attack/superseded_by.jsonl) `d3afa6f7699d`
- [`data/attack/group_to_technique.jsonl`](https://github.com/TeamStarWolf/TeamStarWolf/blob/main/data/attack/group_to_technique.jsonl) `0547008fc1f3`
- [`data/attack/software_to_technique.jsonl`](https://github.com/TeamStarWolf/TeamStarWolf/blob/main/data/attack/software_to_technique.jsonl) `d118560fab51`
- [`data/attack/mitigation_to_technique.jsonl`](https://github.com/TeamStarWolf/TeamStarWolf/blob/main/data/attack/mitigation_to_technique.jsonl) `d027c2a6cf26`

Only live v19.2 techniques are counted. A group, software, mitigation or NIST control edge keyed on an id that ATT&CK v19 revoked is counted under the live successor recorded in [`superseded_by.jsonl`](https://github.com/TeamStarWolf/TeamStarWolf/blob/main/data/attack/superseded_by.jsonl) (for example, the CTID NIST 800-53 mappings keyed on the revoked T1562.001 count under T1685), so a revoked id never appears in the ranking.

A technique in several tactics is counted in each, so the rows do not sum to the live total.

> 231 of the 697 live Enterprise v19.2 techniques have no mapped NIST 800-53 control, under their own id or a revoked predecessor's; see the [framework blind-spots Navigator layer](https://github.com/TeamStarWolf/TeamStarWolf/blob/main/navigator/analytics/no_nist_coverage.json). The CTID mapping targets ATT&CK v16.1, so a technique added since then that does not succeed a mapped id has no control mapping by construction.

### How to use this

1. Start at the top: these techniques combine heavy real-world use with thin control coverage.
2. For each, pull its detections from the [Technique Detection Library](/detections/TECHNIQUE_DETECTION_LIBRARY.md) (or write them), validate with [Atomic Red Team](https://github.com/redcanaryco/atomic-red-team), and add compensating controls where NIST coverage is thin.
3. Track closure over time: after the data changes, run `python scripts/build_priority_gaps.py` to regenerate this page, its JSON and the analytics Navigator layers.

*Source: MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise v19.2 (STIX) + CTID NIST 800-53 R5 -> ATT&CK mappings. Priority is a coverage heuristic, not a substitute for environment-specific risk assessment.*
